target.name: IRAK1 recruits IKK complex
target.description: Innate immune receptors of the interleukin-1 and Toll-like receptor families must convert ligand binding into NF-kappaB-driven transcription of inflammatory genes, and the step in which IRAK1 recruits the IKK complex is where the receptor-proximal signal is physically coupled to the kinase that frees NF-kappaB. target.name: Mismatch repair (MMR) directed by MSH2:MSH6 (MutSalpha)
target.description: Replication inevitably leaves behind mispaired bases and small insertion-deletion loops, and this branch of post-replicative mismatch repair is the route by which single base mismatches and one- to two-nucleotide loops are found and corrected. target.name: atrioventricular node development
target.description: The atrioventricular node is the electrical relay of the heart: it receives the impulse generated by the sinoatrial node, delays it long enough for the atria to empty, then passes it to the His-Purkinje system so the ventricles contract in sequence. Building this small population of specialised conduction myocytes depends on the genes collected here, and when the programme fails the result is heart block, conduction delay and arrhythmia, often alongside septal defects.

target.name: parental behavior
target.description: Parental behavior covers the caregiving a parent directs at offspring infant retrieval, nest building, grooming, nursing and defence and it is one of the few behaviours whose failure is measured in the survival of the next generation rather than of the animal itself.
